subject: Taxes
title: The Revolving Door
description: A quick, practical guide to The Revolving Door.

hook.text: Over half of former members of Congress who leave office join lobbying firms.

buildup.text: Former IRS commissioners, Treasury officials, and tax staffers command huge fees from firms seeking tax advantages.

discovery.text: These former officials understand the tax code intimately.

twist.text: There's a cooling-off period: 1–2 years where former officials can't directly lobby.

climax.text: The revolving door ensures tax expertise flows to those who can pay. Public service creates private advantage.

punchline.text: Write the law, then get paid to navigate it. The revolving door spins.

quiz.question: Why are former government tax officials valuable to lobbying firms?
options: They wrote the tax laws and understand every loophole they created
